4.14 Validation Message Requirements BRULE-61: Clear Validation Feedback When a request fails validation, the system must provide a clear and meaningful error response identifying the reason for rejection. BRULE-62: Consistent Error Handling Validation failures, missing references, state violations, and unauthorized access must be handled consistently across modules. 4.15 Cross-Module Consistency Rules BRULE-63: Downstream Dependency Protection A record must not be changed in a way that invalidates already completed downstream processing unless reversal logic exists. BRULE-64: Operational-to-Financial Continuity Operational records and financial records must remain connected throughout the lifecycle of a business transaction. BRULE-65: No Contradictory States The system must not allow a business record to exist in mutually contradictory states across related modules. Example • A job cannot be treated as closed for operations while remaining openly editable for dependent services without explicit business support. • A voided invoice cannot simultaneously behave as an active collectible invoice. 4.16 Acceptance of Business Rules The business rules in this section are considered satisfied when: • the system enforces the defined conditions before processing transactions,

4. Business Rules and Validation Requirements 4.1 Overview This section defines the business rules, validation rules, and operational constraints that govern the behavior of the LogisticsPro API. These rules ensure that the system processes data consistently, preserves business integrity, and prevents invalid or contradictory operations. Business rules are mandatory conditions derived from the business domain. They apply across modules such as master data management, job processing, operational services, financial processing, and reporting. Validation requirements define the checks that must be applied to incoming data before business transactions are accepted. The purpose of this section is to remove ambiguity from the functional requirements by stating exactly what conditions must hold true before a process can be executed, what transitions are allowed, and what actions must be restricted. 4.2 Rule Classification The business rules in this document are grouped into the following categories: • General system rules • Authentication and access rules • Master data rules • Job card lifecycle rules • Operational service rules • Cost and calculation rules • Batch processing rules • Payment voucher rules • Invoice and proforma invoice rules • Receipt rules
